subject: Tenant isolation and KMS patterns for edge/private deployments
body:
From: Alice Wang <alice.wang@fintegrity.io>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: KMS patterns for on-prem tenant isolation (Fintegrity)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The infosec team at Fintegrity has a few follow-ups about our private deployment options. Two quick asks: (1) we need a recommended key custody pattern that supports BYOK where our HSM (Thales) remains the root of trust, and (2) confirmation on network egress requirements so keys are never exposed off our VPC. Can you share a short write-up or diagram we can pass to our SecureOps folks?

Also – rotation cadence and audit log retention (we need 7 years) will be gating for our procurement.

Appreciate it,
Alice
---

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Wang <alice.wang@fintegrity.io>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: KMS patterns for on-prem tenant isolation (Fintegrity)

Team — forwarding Fintegrity's ask. High level we should propose two patterns: (A) Customer-hosted HSM with Redwood connector (we never hold root keys), and (B) Redwood-managed KMS in their VPC with customer-supplied key material wrapped by HSM.

Immediate asks:
- Laura: can you draft the short diagram/text for the SecureOps audience? Keep it 1 page.
- Mina: confirm whether our agent can run in a private subnet (no egress) and still perform signing/unwrap ops over internal VPC endpoints.
- Marcus: need SRE input on rotation tooling and audit retention SLAs.

I'll attach the current draft patterns and schedule a quick sync with Fintegrity for Monday.

Thanks,
Rishi

On Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0400, laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Wang <alice.wang@fintegrity.io>
Subject: Re: KMS patterns for on-prem tenant isolation (Fintegrity)

Rishi / all — initial 1-pager for SecureOps attached. I focused on clear guarantees: no plaintext key egress, HSM-isolated root of trust, and two recommended flows (BYOK direct HSM and wrapped-key flow).

Key bullets:
- BYOK direct HSM (customer-run): Redwood installs a connector (container) in customer's private subnet. All key operations (Generate, Sign/Decrypt) are proxied to the customer HSM via mTLS and do not leave the VPC. Redwood holds ephemeral wrapping keys only for session management and does not persist root key material.
- Wrapped-key model (customer supplies key material): Customer exports key material under HSM policy, uploads wrapped blob to Redwood over a mutually authenticated channel. Redwood performs per-tenant unwrap into an in-memory key cache with strict TTL and re-asks HSM for rewrap on rotation windows.
- Rotation: recommend 90-day rewrap cadence for sym keys, yearly rotation for root material (customer policy dependent). Support for ad-hoc rotation on demand via API.
- Audit: all KMS calls logged with tenant id, operation type, and request signature. Logs are shipped to customer's SIEM via a push endpoint or pulled via secure s3 with MFA. Retention configurable; default 7y if requested (note cost impact).

I added a simple network diagram (see PNG). Next steps: confirm connector egress needs and whether Fintegrity's Thales supports the session patterns below.

Laura
[Attachment: hsm-integration-diagram.png (image/png)]

On Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:14:00 -0400, mina_haddad@redwood.ai wrote:
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Wang <alice.wang@fintegrity.io>
Subject: Re: KMS patterns for on-prem tenant isolation (Fintegrity)

Checked with infra: connector can run in a private subnet with 0.0.0.0/0 blocked, but needs outbound to specific HSM management endpoints (TCP/2181 and TCP/443) depending on vendor. If Fintegrity strictly disallows any outbound, we can route through an approved NAT with strict allowlists and mTLS to the HSM cluster; the important part is that key material never leaves HSM hardware unencrypted.

Notes:
- Connector will maintain ephemeral in-memory caches only; we will not write unwrapped keys to disk.
- For wrapped-key model, unwrapping happens in-memory and we enforce an attestation token from the HSM before accepting unwrapped material.
- We can offer an air-gapped install option where Redwood engineers run the connector as a managed appliance on-prem (requires RSA-based signing between the appliance and control plane).

Mina

On Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0400, marcus_lin@redwood.ai wrote:
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Wang <alice.wang@fintegrity.io>
Subject: Re: KMS patterns for on-prem tenant isolation (Fintegrity)

Quick SRE input:
- Rotation automation: we have a scheduler that can trigger rotation events and call the HSM APIs for rewrap. We'll need an SLA for rotation completion (target <10m for symmetric keys when HSM is reachable).
- Audit retention: we can archive signed audit bundles to the customer's object store with server-side encryption using keys they control. 7-year retention is feasible but adds storage & indexing cost; recommend estimating based on expected ops/tokens.
- High availability: recommend a multi-AZ HSM cluster and two connector instances in separate subnets for failover. Ensure HSM client libraries are pinned to vetted versions.

I'll prepare a short note for procurement that outlines failure modes and fallback (if HSM unavailable, fallback to a pre-approved wrapped-key cached for X minutes with throttling).

Marcus

On Sun, 15 Aug 2026 17:40:00 -0400, Alice Wang <alice.wang@fintegrity.io> wrote:
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: KMS patterns for on-prem tenant isolation (Fintegrity)

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail SecureOps asked for. A couple of clarifying Qs before I share with procurement: 

1) For the BYOK direct HSM pattern, can you confirm that Redwood never has access to the root key material and that all audit logs referencing key IDs are exportable to our SIEM?
2) For wrapped-key flow, who holds the long-term unwrapped key if we request emergency unwrapping for disaster recovery?
3) Can you provide an example SLA line for rotation completion and maximum outage during a rotation (we need something we can insert into the MSA).

If you prefer, we can do a 20m call Monday morning to finalize. Otherwise I'll share the docs with SecureOps later today.

Best,
Alice
